clue: Serum sodium level less than 135 mEq/L
rationale: Chapter mnemonic for its manifestations: SALT LOSS.

clue: Below-normal serum potassium, less than 3.5 mEq/L
rationale: Chapter mnemonic: "7 Ls — low and slow."

clue: Serum calcium level less than 8.6 mg/dL
rationale: Chapter mnemonic: CRAMPS; watch for tetany and positive Trousseau/Chvostek signs.

clue: Serum magnesium level less than 1.8 mg/dL
rationale: Chapter mnemonic: TWITCH; associated with hypokalemia and hypocalcemia.

clue: Serum magnesium level greater than 2.6 mg/dL
rationale: Chapter mnemonic: LETHARGIC; rare because the kidneys efficiently excrete magnesium.

clue: ___ sign: paired with Chvostek sign in the chapter's hypocalcemia and hypomagnesemia findings
rationale: Named under both imbalances' clinical manifestations lists.

clue: Movement of water from an area of low solute concentration to an area of high solute concentration
rationale: One of four fluid-regulation mechanisms in the chapter's "Regulation of Fluid" section.

clue: Movement of solutes from an area of higher concentration to one of lower concentration
rationale: Also listed under "Regulation of Fluid."

clue: Movement of water and solutes from an area of high hydrostatic pressure to an area of low hydrostatic pressure
rationale: Third of the chapter's four fluid-regulation mechanisms.

clue: Loss of water alone with increased serum sodium levels — explicitly not the same as fluid volume deficit
rationale: The chapter draws this distinction directly: FVD loses electrolytes in the same proportion as water.

clue: Ion regulated by the kidneys as part of the ECF's major buffer system
rationale: Named in the bicarbonate–carbonic acid buffer system; normal ABG range given as 22–26 mEq/L.

clue: The chapter's alternate name for fluid volume deficit
rationale: Occurs when loss of extracellular fluid exceeds intake.

clue: The chapter's alternate name for fluid volume excess
rationale: Abnormal retention of water and sodium in roughly normal ECF proportions.

clue: Hormone named in the chapter's Renin–Angiotensin–___ System
rationale: Listed among the body's homeostatic mechanisms for fluid balance.

clue: ECF subtype that surrounds the cell, e.g. lymph
rationale: One of three ECF subtypes listed, with intravascular and transcellular.

clue: ECF subtype within blood vessels: plasma, erythrocytes, leukocytes, thrombocytes
rationale: One of three ECF subtypes the chapter lists.

clue: Clinical manifestation of fluid volume excess, along with distended neck veins and crackles
rationale: Listed first among FVE's clinical manifestations.

clue: Metabolic ___: low pH under 7.35 with plasma bicarbonate under 22 mEq/L
rationale: With this condition, hyperkalemia may occur as potassium shifts out of the cell.

clue: Metabolic ___: high pH over 7.45 with high bicarbonate over 26 mEq/L
rationale: Hypokalemia will produce this condition, per the chapter.

clue: Abnormal tingling/numbness sensation listed as a manifestation of hypokalemia and hypocalcemia
rationale: Appears in the clinical manifestations lists for multiple electrolyte imbalances.

clue: Major cation whose imbalance causes ECG changes and dysrhythmias
rationale: Listed among the chapter's major cations, along with sodium, calcium, and magnesium.

clue: Major cation regulated via the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system
rationale: Listed among the chapter's major cations.

clue: Major cation whose deficiency is associated with hypokalemia and hypocalcemia
rationale: Listed among the chapter's major cations.

clue: Major anion listed alongside bicarbonate, phosphate, and sulfate
rationale: One of the chapter's major anions.
